title: Talking About Mental Health
objective: After this level you can explain how to talk about mental health without stigma and where to point someone who needs help.
summary: Stigma keeps people from seeking help. Person-first, non-stigmatizing language helps, asking directly about suicide is safe, and in the US the 988 Lifeline is a call or text away.

cards.headline: The words people use can make asking for help harder, or easier.
cards.body: Stigma, negative attitudes about mental illness, has a real cost: it makes people reluctant to seek help or to stay with treatment. How you talk is one thing you can change today.

cards.headline: Three kinds of stigma
cards.body: Public stigma is the negative attitudes other people hold. Self-stigma is when a person turns those attitudes inward, as shame about their own condition. Structural stigma lives in policies that limit opportunities. Together they make people reluctant to seek help, or to stay with treatment once they start.

items.label: Person first
points: Puts the person before the diagnosis

cards.headline: Where to point someone
cards.body: If you're worried someone is thinking about suicide, NIMH says asking them directly can be the best way to find out, and studies show asking doesn't increase suicidal thoughts. In the United States, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, launched in July 2022, offers free, confidential support around the clock: call or text 988. It's for anyone in emotional distress, not only a crisis. For ongoing help, Level 2's psychologists and counselors provide therapy.

mascot.line: If you remember one thing: asking directly is safe, and in the US, 988 is a call or text away.

cards.headline: Talking with care
learned: Stigma makes people reluctant to seek help

questions.prompt: Which of these phrases do mental health groups advise against?

options.label: "That's so surprising"
options.rationale: That's the suggested swap for casual "crazy".

questions.explanation: NIMH advises avoiding "committing suicide"; "died by suicide" is recommended instead.

questions.prompt: You're worried a coworker who seems very low may be thinking about suicide. What does research say about asking them directly?

options.label: Asking can plant the idea, so avoid it
options.rationale: Studies show asking doesn't increase suicidal thoughts.

options.label: Asking is safe and can help find out
Only a psychiatrist is allowed to ask
options.rationale: NIMH encourages anyone worried to ask directly.

options.label: Wait until they bring it up first
options.rationale: Asking directly can be the best way to identify risk.

questions.explanation: NIMH: asking directly can be the best way to identify someone at risk, and it does not increase suicidal thoughts.

questions.prompt: A friend wants ongoing talk therapy. Using Level 2, which professionals provide therapy?

options.label: Only psychiatrists, because therapy needs a medical degree
options.rationale: Psychologists and counselors provide therapy too.

options.label: Psychologists, psychiatrists and counselors can all provide it
Only forensic psychologists
options.rationale: They work in the justice system.

options.label: No one with a license; only friends and family

questions.explanation: Psychologists, psychiatrists and counselors all provide therapy; only psychiatrists can prescribe medication.
